title: Dynamic Inventory Stock Updates
business: Retail warehouse managers needing real-time visibility into stock levels without complex frontend state management.
problem: Traditional page reloads for stock checks are slow, while building a full JavaScript SPA to handle partial updates introduces significant maintenance overhead and complexity.
solution: htmx allows the server to push HTML fragments directly to specific DOM elements, enabling reactive UI updates through standard HTML attributes without writing custom JavaScript.
steps: Identify the container element in the HTML that displays the current stock count.
Add the hx-get attribute to a refresh button pointing to the server endpoint that returns the updated stock HTML fragment.
Set the hx-target attribute to the ID of the stock display container.
Configure the hx-swap attribute to replace the innerHTML of the target element with the new server response.
outcome: The inventory dashboard remains responsive and displays current data with minimal code, maintaining a clean separation between server-side logic and client-side presentation.
limitation: Because htmx relies on server-side HTML generation, high-frequency updates can increase server load; verify this by monitoring the frequency of requests and the size of the returned HTML fragments.
